question: Is a foreign employee who works in Malaysia for less than 60 days taxed on their employment income?
answer_notes: Exempt if employment period in Malaysia does not exceed 60 days (para 21, Schedule 6 ITA).
answer: No, employment income derived by a non-resident individual from exercising employment in Malaysia is generally exempt from tax pursuant to paragraph 21 of Schedule 6 of the ITA if the employment period or periods together do not exceed 60 days in a basis year for a year of assessment [1][3]. However, the tax exemption will not apply if the employment period in Malaysia amounts to more than 60 days in a basis year, or if a continuous period exceeding 60 days overlaps two successive basis periods [5]. For this purpose, the 60-day period refers to the period of employment in Malaysia rather than physical presence [2].
cited_titles: Public Ruling No. 2/2026: Tax Treatment of Foreign Nationals Exercising Employment in Malaysia

question: What tax rate applies to a foreign national who is not tax resident in Malaysia?
answer_notes: Section 4.5: residents taxed at scale rates with reliefs; non-residents at a flat rate without reliefs.
answer: Non-resident individuals are subject to tax at a flat rate of 30% on every ringgit of the chargeable income, as specified in paragraph 1A, Part 1 of Schedule 1 to the ITA [1]. Special tax rates for an individual under certain incentives may also apply as specified in Part XIV and XVIII of Schedule 1 to the ITA [1].
cited_titles: Public Ruling No. 2/2026: Tax Treatment of Foreign Nationals Exercising Employment in Malaysia

answer_notes: No — section 13: special allowances do not apply to assets acquired on hire purchase; normal capital allowance instead.

question: What purchases qualify for lifestyle relief?
answer_notes: Section 6.11: books/journals/magazines/newspapers, personal computer/smartphone/tablet, internet subscription, skills courses.
answer: Under paragraph 46(1)(p) of the ITA, lifestyle relief qualifies for expenses incurred by an individual for the use of himself, his spouse, or children for: (a) the purchase of books, journals, magazines, newspapers, and other similar publications (including school textbooks, e-books, periodicals, and comics, whether local or overseas, but excluding banned reading materials) for enhancing knowledge [4]; (b) the purchase of a personal computer, smartphone, or tablet (not used for business purposes) [4]; (c) the payment of monthly internet subscription bills registered under the individual's name or the use of their spouse or child [2]; and (d) effective from YA 2024, self-enrichment course fees (limited to courses attended by the individual only, encouraging skills unrelated to their job such as hobbies, religion, or languages) [2]. Expenses for gym memberships and tennis rackets are not eligible under this lifestyle relief provision [5].
cited_titles: Public Ruling No. 5/2026: Taxation of a Resident Individual Part I - Gifts or Contributions and Allowable Deductions

question: What conditions must be met to claim tax relief for breastfeeding equipment?
answer_notes: Section 6.12.3: breastfeeding mother, child up to 2 years, equipment for own use, receipts.
answer: To claim a tax deduction for the purchase of breastfeeding equipment, an individual must meet the following conditions: (a) be a breastfeeding mother [1]; (b) breastfeed her child aged up to 2 years [1]; (c) expend on the purchase of breastfeeding equipment for her own use [1]; and (d) make a claim evidenced by receipts issued in respect of the purchase [1]. Additionally, for the case of a combined assessment, the deduction is allowed where the assessment is made in the name of the wife [2]. The deduction is allowed once in every two YAs [1][3].
cited_titles: Public Ruling No. 5/2026: Taxation of a Resident Individual Part I - Gifts or Contributions and Allowable Deductions

question: How much service tax is charged on a credit card?
answer_notes: RM25 per card on activation and every 12 months thereafter.
answer: The rate of service tax for the provision of credit line facility or shariah compliance financing services through the activation or renewal of a primary credit card, primary charge card, supplementary credit card, or supplementary charge card is RM25.00 for each card, applicable on the date the card is activated and every 12 months thereafter or part thereof [2]. This service tax of RM25 per card activation or annual card renewal applies regardless of whether any annual card fee is imposed [3].

question: Is service tax charged on financial services imported from a foreign provider?
answer_notes: Imported taxable financial services section (paragraph 28 onwards).
answer: Yes, recipients in Malaysia are obligated to account for and pay service tax on imported taxable services (including financial advisory services) if the services are used for the purpose of their business and are taxable when made in Malaysia [1][4]. The foreign service provider is not required to charge the service tax; instead, the tax responsibility is shifted to the recipient in Malaysia [5]. However, financial services acquired from abroad by registered financial service providers are eligible for tax exemption [2].
cited_titles: Service Tax Guide on Financial Services (Version 2)

question: Which private education providers are subject to service tax from 1 July 2025?
answer_notes: Paragraph 22: private playschools, kindergartens, primary and secondary schools, tuition and learning centres, international and expatriate schools.
answer: Service tax is imposed from 1 July 2025 on education services for private playschools, private kindergartens, private primary schools, private secondary schools, tuition centres, learning centres, international schools, and expatriate schools [3]. Additionally, service tax is imposed on non-Malaysian citizens who acquire education services in Malaysia from private universities, colleges, university colleges, and language centres [3].
